content.intended_use: Identify when the all-budget envelope becomes a matching statistical characterization.

proofs.full_local_argument: Import c_p H(min(G,w))<=E<=C_p H(min(G,v)) from the linked all-budget theorem. For a>=0, H is nondecreasing. For 0<c<=1, substituting rho=c t in its defining maximum gives H(ca)>=c^2 H(a), and comparing c a rho-mu rho^2/2<=c(a rho-mu rho^2/2) gives H(ca)<=c H(a). Thus for lambda>=1, H(lambda a)<=lambda^2 H(a). If w>=G, both capped amplitudes equal G and the saturation conclusion follows. If v-w<=C0 w, let a=min(G,w), b=min(G,v); then a<=b<=(1+C0)a, so the envelope gives E comparable_{p,C0} H(a). For the sufficient domination condition, G/sqrt(T)<=L/sqrt(T), while T>=(G/L)^2 ell^2 implies G ell/T<=L/sqrt(T); both are bounded by w. If mu>0 and w<=min(G,mu D), H(w)=w^2/(2mu). Writing x=L/sqrt(T), y=s((e+ell)/T)^q, x^2+y^2<=(x+y)^2<=2(x^2+y^2), and (e+ell)^(2q) comparable_p to e^(2q)+ell^(2q), gives the full quadratic formula. For Theorem 2.1, w>=u and v<= (1+C0)u by its domination condition; u<=G implies min(G,w)>=u and min(G,v)<=(1+C0)u. The same H comparison yields E comparable_{p,C0} H(u). For mu=0, H(u)=Du; for mu>0 with u<=mu D, H(u)=u^2/(2mu). Finally (e+ell)^q is comparable_p to e^q+ell^q, and the same square comparison gives the two displayed heavy-tail rates. This argument derives only the stated consequences of the imported envelope.

assumptions: Known nonempty closed convex X subset R^d; unknown convex G-Lipschitz f; known mu-strongly convex r; h=r+indicator_X proper closed convex with exact prox for every positive parameter. F has minimizer x* and supplied feasible x1 satisfies ||x1-x*||<=D.

A fixed query-dependent kernel gives fresh unbiased subgradients, independent of prior history conditional on the query. Centered noise obeys conditional E||zeta||^p<=L^p and sup_{||v||=1}E|<v,zeta>|^p<=s^p separately, at every adaptive query.

All public parameters and known X,r are available. Unknown values and reusable random functions are unavailable; deterministic known-object operations and prox are uncharged, internal computation unrestricted. Every rejected observation counts as a raw call.
For Theorem 2.1, d>=ceil(e), u_T<=G, and G/sqrt(T)+G ell/T+L/sqrt(T)<=C0 u_T for fixed C0>0. Its strong-convexity conclusion additionally requires mu>0 and u_T<=mu D.

For Corollary 2.3, d>=ceil(e). Its matching nonsaturated assertion requires G/sqrt(T)+G ell/T<=C0 w_T; its saturation assertion instead assumes w_T>=G. Its full quadratic-rate specialization additionally assumes mu>0 and w_T<=min{G,mu D}.
statement.conclusion: Theorem 2.1: E_T^(0)(delta) is comparable_{p,C0} to D(A+s ell^q)/T^q. Under its additional strong-convexity conditions, E_T^(mu)(delta) is comparable_{p,C0} to (A^2+s^2 ell^(2q))/(mu T^(2q)). Corollary 2.3: if w_T>=G then E_T^(mu)(delta) is comparable_p to H(G). If G/sqrt(T)+G ell/T<=C0 w_T, then E_T^(mu)(delta) is comparable_{p,C0} to H(min{G,w_T}). A sufficient condition for this domination with an absolute C0 is L>=G and T>=(G/L)^2 ell^2. If additionally mu>0 and w_T<=min{G,mu D}, its full quadratic statistical rate is comparable_{p,C0} to (1/mu)[L^2/T+(A^2+s^2 ell^(2q))/T^(2q)]. Theorem 2.1's reduced formulas require domination of L/sqrt(T); Corollary 2.3 retains that term.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Use Euclidean F=f+r on known X with exact prox_{eta(r+indicator_X)}. E_T^(mu)(delta)=inf_{A: raw calls<=T almost surely} inf{epsilon>=0:sup_I P_I(F_I(xhat_A)-F_I*)>epsilon)<=delta}, where the probability notation means sup_I P_I{F_I(xhat_A)-F_I*>epsilon}<=delta. Set q=1-1/p, e=L^2/s^2, A=s e^q, ell=log(3/delta), K=e+ell, u_T=s(K/T)^q, w_T=L/sqrt(T)+u_T, v_T=G/sqrt(T)+G ell/T+w_T. H(a)=max_{0<=rho<=D}(a rho-mu rho^2/2).
statement.parameter_domains: 1<p<=2; G,D>0; 0<s<=L; mu>=0; integer T>=1; 0<delta<1/10; finite integer d>=ceil(e); C0>0 fixed for domination branches.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every admissible parameter tuple satisfying each indicated branch's conditions, comparisons hold with positive constants depending only on p,C0 (only p in the saturation assertion). Risk includes oracle and internal algorithm randomness. Lower comparisons cover arbitrary adaptive randomized algorithms; upper witnesses use unrestricted computation and public-parameter procedure selection.
